_comment: Known IPC registration gaps at gate introduction (F-008/F-050). Entries are UI command strings not yet registered in that shell; they shrink to zero as F-006 removes the dead surface. Stale entries (command now registered) fail the gate. create_backup_scoped / get_backup_status_scoped joined with 5f0692e1: DataManagementScreen now prefers the permission-checked twins, but the tablet shell registers no data surface at all -- create_backup, get_backup_status, export_data, import_data and import_preview were already listed here. The unscoped names stay, because the ADR #7 conditional still falls back to them when no session token exists. pick_logo_file_scoped joined the same way: AppearanceSettings now prefers the SETTINGS_EDIT-checked twin, and the tablet shell registers neither variant. pause_subscription_scoped / resume_subscription_scoped joined the same way: LicenseSettings now prefers the SETTINGS_EDIT-checked twins, and the tablet shell registers neither variant of either command. get_report_schedule_scoped joined the same way: EmailReportSettings now prefers the REPORTS_SCHEDULE-checked twin, and the tablet shell registers neither variant. The legal-entity commands were initially allowlisted with bcd1f501 while the tablet shell had no implementation; they are removed from this list once the shared command module is registered in the tablet shell. The three memo-authoring entries (create_memo_scoped, list_authored_memos_scoped, publish_memo_scoped) are a deliberate product choice, not a gap: authoring is desktop-only (the back-office manager writes Memos; the tablet's Memo surface is the display banner), following the legal-entity precedent of desktop-first authoring IPC. stop_memo_scoped and revise_memo_scoped join them for the same reason (the 2026-09-07 A2/scope rulings): early-stopping and corrections are management actions on the authoring screen (MemosScreen is registry-gated to manager+ on desktop), and the tablet shell has no management surface. All five come off this list only if Memo authoring/management is ever ported to the tablet shell. The two §J quota-remediation commands (suspend_surplus_workspace_instances_scoped, recover_workspace_instances_scoped) joined on 2026-09-09 for the same reason the memo entries did, and by the route the scoped_orphans comment prescribes: they sat in scoped_orphans as permission checks guarding nothing until B1 gave them a caller in the shared over-quota card, and this shell does not register them. Quota remediation is a back-office owner action on a tenant-level view, so this is a recorded product choice and not a gap. They come off this list when the tablet shell registers them - and, per the same rule, they must never leave one list without appearing in another.
_scoped_orphans_comment: Scoped commands registered in a shell's generate_handler! that no client invokes, accepted as host-only. Each entry is a permission check that currently guards nothing, so this list is a work queue, not a clean bill of health. An entry that gains a caller fails the gate as stale. The memo authoring entries (create/publish/list_authored) are NOT host-only orphans — the authoring screen now invokes all three from the shared api (3fb745cf), so they left this list and moved to the tablet allowlist with a recorded product choice: authoring is desktop-only, following the legal-entity precedent. They return here only if tablet registration would leave them caller-less again. The four payables entries (create/list/record_payment/write_off) are the desktop-only AP authoring surface landed ahead of its UI: the Hutang screen is a later slice, so these commands currently have no caller at all (unlike memo authoring, which already has one). They leave this list when the payables UI wires them, exactly as the memo entries did. `list_security_events_scoped` left this list on 2026-09-09, when its caller landed in `ui/src/api/audit.ts` — it was never host-only, just early, and the exit condition recorded here is the one it met. It is NOT clean: the same command now sits under `dev_mock` because the browser mock still has no handler. Moving between these two lists is the honest bookkeeping; disappearing from both is not the same claim.
_dev_mock_comment: UI command strings that ui/src/dev-mock/tauri-api.ts cannot answer: no handler of its own and no unscoped twin for the alias rule to reach, so invoke() resolves to null in browser dev preview. That silent null is the R36-02 failure mode the mock itself warns about, so every entry here is recorded debt, not a clean pass. Entries appear when a slice adds a UI caller while dev-mock -- a hot file owned by another stream -- has no handler yet; the gap is recorded rather than editing that file. An entry fails the gate as stale the moment a handler appears, which is what makes the list self-clearing. list_role_holders_scoped was the first entry here — added 2026-09-08 with the role-holders slice, when the command was registered and gated (staff:read) in both shells with a live caller and no mock — and cleared 2026-09-09 once dev-mock gained its handler. It is the only entry that has ever self-cleared, which is the point of the staleness check: an entry that outlives its gap makes the gate lie in the other direction. list_security_events_scoped joined 2026-09-09 with the audit security-events UI half, and is the SAME command moving lists rather than new debt: it left scoped_orphans the day its caller landed, so the remaining gap is only the browser mock. Note what its null resolved to there, because it was not benign in the way an empty list would be — the backend refuses a Free tier outright, so a browser preview could not distinguish tier refusal from a transport failure and would always show the failure path. It cleared on 2026-09-09 with SecurityTrailScreen: the handler returns a plausible page and honors the outcome and query args, so the preview exercises the same filtering the real command does server-side. What the list still cannot see is a handler with the WRONG SHAPE. export_audit_log_scoped returned an empty string to an object DTO and mark_audit_reviewed_scoped returned null to one; get_audit_review_status_scoped was NOT a shape violation (its checkpoint/unreviewed_count pair matched AuditReviewStatusDto exactly) but was inert, hard-coding a null checkpoint and a zero count so a review could never be previewed. All three were corrected 2026-09-09 and are pinned by ui/src/__tests__/dev-mock-audit-shapes.test.ts against the Rust field names rather than against the mock. That test also caught a subtler sibling of the same class: invoke() hands a handler args?.['args'] ?? args, so a handler that reads args.args receives nothing and silently ignores every filter — list_security_events_scoped did exactly that when it was written here, under a comment claiming it honored them. A mock can therefore lie about its OUTPUT, its INPUT, or its INERTNESS, and this gate has only ever been asked about absence.
